study.research_problem: A newly adopted calcar-guided short femoral stem requires post-market surveillance because its bone-preserving/proximal-loading rationale does not itself establish durable survival or patient benefit.
study.exact_gap: Only limited mid-term Optimys data existed, so a larger multicenter cohort was needed to estimate five-year revision-defined survival and describe early patient-reported recovery.
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Estimate five-year Optimys stem survival and the trajectory of HOOS, SF-36, and satisfaction in a broad elective-THA cohort.
study.study_design: Prospective consecutive two-center single-arm cohort enrolled from 2014-2021, with clinical follow-up, registry/file revision ascertainment, Kaplan-Meier survival, and mixed-model PROM trajectories.
study.sample_or_model: 500 adults receiving the same Ti6Al4V plasma-sprayed/calcium-phosphate-coated Optimys stem; mean age 62.3 years, 40% male; ASA greater than 3, sepsis, malignancy, and revision cases excluded.
comparators: No concurrent stem or conventional-THA comparator
All-cause revision versus infection-excluded stem revision
Contextual comparison with published cohorts and NICE ten-year benchmark
method_spine: Define the consecutive eligible population and revision endpoint.
Ascertain revision through files and the national registry.
Estimate five-year survival with censoring and confidence intervals.
Model PROM change in years one and two and expose response denominators.
Contextualize rather than causally compare against external cohorts/benchmarks.

verification: Patient files plus the LROI registry cross-check revision status, although registry reason fields are incomplete (S003:C01; S010:C04).
validation: The cohort provides prospective post-market survival and PROM evidence for the specific stem; it does not validate the design mechanisms of proximal loading, bone preservation, coating ingrowth, or superiority.
sensitivity: Last-observation-carried-forward sensitivity yielded smaller first-year PROM effects but a similar qualitative trajectory; it does not remove nonresponse bias (S006:C01; S009:C01).
application_prediction: Expected compliance with a ten-year NICE revision benchmark and safety for common daily use are projections from five-year uncontrolled data (S010:C01; S014:C01-S017:C01).

primary_outcomes: At median 5.5-year follow-up, six revisions and seven deaths in situ yielded 98.8% five-year all-cause revision-free survival (95% CI 97.3-99.5) (S008:C01).

Three revisions were for infection, two for subsidence attributed to undersizing, and one for malposition; infection-excluded survival was 99.4% (95% CI 98.1-99.8), with no revision labeled aseptic loosening (S008:C01).

PROM response fell from 471/500 at baseline to 317/500 at one year and 233/500 at two years; all domains improved during year one and showed no significant additional change during year two (S009:C01-S009:C03).
Only 210/500 supplied two-year satisfaction, among whom 91.4% were satisfied or very satisfied (S009:C03).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Moderate-size prospective single-arm device-surveillance evidence with few revision events and substantial PROM attrition; no comparative effectiveness or direct osseointegration evidence.

argument_map.central_claim: The Optimys stem showed high five-year revision-free survival in this selected two-center cohort and large early PROM improvement, but absence of a comparator, few events, incomplete PROM follow-up, and lack of direct mechanical/bone endpoints prevent claims of superiority, mechanism, or established long-term safety.
data: Kaplan-Meier estimate, confidence interval, and reasons for six revisions (S008:C01).
Repeated HOOS/SF-36 values with explicit declining denominators and mixed-model estimates (S009:C01-S009:C03).
argument_map.warrant: A device-survival claim is justified by revision ascertainment and time-to-event analysis; claims about why the device survives or whether it is better require mechanistic or concurrent comparative data.
backing: Results are broadly similar to external short-stem cohorts, but these are contextual rather than exchangeable controls (S010:C02-S010:C04).
argument_map.qualifier: Five-year, revision-defined, selected elective population at two Dutch centers.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: No randomized or parallel conventional-stem group.
Six total events produce wide uncertainty about specific failure modes despite a narrow overall survival interval.
PROM response is 47% at two years and satisfaction response 42%, permitting informative missingness.
Revision-free status does not measure radiographic migration, bone remodeling, BIC, interface mechanics, pain-free function, or future wear.
The five-year curve cannot establish a ten-year benchmark, and exclusions limit high-risk generalizability.

measured: Population characteristics, observed revisions/deaths, registry/file follow-up, HOOS, SF-36, and respondent satisfaction (S003:C01-S009:C03).
predicted: Ten-year benchmark compliance is informally projected from five-year experience without a formal extrapolation model (S010:C01).
inferred: Subsidence is attributed to undersizing with later fixation based on revision observations (S008:C01; S010:C01).
Safety/viability for common use is inferred from single-arm survival and PROMs (S014:C01; S017:C01).
Bone-stock preservation and proximal loading are design rationales, not measured cohort outcomes (S002:C01; S012:C01).
recommended: Continue ten-year follow-up and add comparative, radiographic/migration, bone-remodeling, and subgroup evidence (S010:C04-S010:C05; S018:C01).
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Revision-free survival is a patient-important device endpoint but does not equal radiographic or histological osseointegration.
No aseptic-loosening revision is not proof that every stem was biologically integrated.
PROM improvement after THA cannot be attributed specifically to the short-stem design without a comparator.
Infection-excluded survival answers a device-mechanical question but must not erase infection from all-cause patient risk.
overclaim_risks: The paper calls the population large and varied despite exclusions of ASA greater than 3, sepsis, malignancy, and revision surgery (S003:C01; S014:C01).
'Safe and viable for common use' is stronger than a five-year uncontrolled cohort supports (S017:C01).
Expected NICE compliance at ten years is asserted from five-year results (S010:C01).
The article is labeled/prepared under CONSORT despite being a nonrandomized cohort (S020:C01).

section_moves.execution: Revision is defined, reasons are retained, deaths are censored, and the Kaplan-Meier confidence interval is specified (S005:C01-S006:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: A device-survival paragraph must name the index component, failure event, competing/censoring rules, horizon, denominator, and confidence interval.
section_moves.failure_mode: Changing from all-cause to infection-excluded revision changes the estimand and must remain visibly secondary.

section_moves.move: Carry response denominators beside every longitudinal outcome
section_moves.execution: The paper states baseline, one-year, two-year, and satisfaction denominators before interpreting PROM change (S009:C01-S009:C03).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For repeated PROMs, report n/N at every time point, model assumptions, effect with interval, and an explicit informative-missingness boundary.
section_moves.failure_mode: A sensitivity analysis based on last observation carried forward does not prove missing-at-random or eliminate attrition bias.

section_moves.move: Use external evidence as context, not a synthetic control
section_moves.execution: Other Optimys, NANOS, Fitmore, and systematic-review survival figures are compared narratively (S010:C02-S010:C04).
section_moves.transferable_principle: In a single-arm device cohort, call external benchmarks contextual comparators and list population, component, endpoint, and follow-up incompatibilities before judging similarity.
section_moves.failure_mode: Comparable percentages across nonexchangeable cohorts do not establish noninferiority or superiority.

section_moves.move: Separate device survival, function, and biological mechanism
section_moves.execution: The data report revision and PROMs, while bone preservation, loading, coating ingrowth, and fixation are background rationales (S002:C01; S004:C01; S008:C01-S009:C03).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Keep survival, patient experience, radiographic mechanics, and osseointegration in separate columns; use only verbs supported by the measured column.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not translate 'no aseptic-loosening revision' into measured bone integration or proximal-load preservation.

author_reported: Incomplete registry reason for one revision, low PROM response—especially at two years—and need for long-term survival follow-up (S010:C04-S010:C05).
reader_identified: No concurrent control, radiographic outcomes, RSA/migration data in this cohort, bone density/remodeling, implant-position analysis, or activity/wear assessment.
Only six revision events limit failure-mode precision and multivariable risk assessment.
Approach and likely surgeon/center practice varied but are not modeled.
No formal sample-size rationale, lost-to-follow-up accounting beyond deaths/revisions, or competing-risk analysis is described.
LOCF is a weak missing-data sensitivity analysis and satisfaction is reported among only 42%.
Five-year evidence cannot validate a ten-year benchmark or long-term wear/late loosening.
likely_bias_direction: Informative PROM nonresponse may overestimate or underestimate recovery; satisfied patients may be more likely to respond to satisfaction surveys.
Elective low-to-moderate-risk exclusions likely overestimate general-population performance.
Attribution of all improvement to the stem rather than THA and care pathway likely overstates device-specific benefit.
limitations.scope_boundary: The study estimates revision-defined five-year survival and early patient-reported trajectory for one short stem in selected elective patients; it does not establish comparative superiority, biological osseointegration, bone preservation, or ten-year safety.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write implant survival with a fully specified estimand and keep all-cause, device-specific, infection-excluded, radiographic, and clinical endpoints distinct.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Clinical Methods, Results, abstract, and survival table.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A high infection-excluded survival estimate must not replace all-cause patient risk or imply osseointegration.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Attach longitudinal PROM conclusions to time-specific response denominators, intervals, missingness assumptions, and sensitivity results.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A stable mean among remaining respondents does not establish stable recovery in all enrolled patients.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Separate measured device survival and patient benefit from unmeasured design rationales such as proximal loading, bone preservation, coating ingrowth, and biological fixation.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Introduction rationale, Discussion, and conclusion audit.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Revision-free follow-up is compatible with, but does not directly measure, the proposed biomechanical mechanism.

critical_weaknesses: Single arm and only six events.
PROM response falls to 47% and satisfaction to 42%.

summary_zh: 这篇队列最适合提炼的是临床植入器械结局的分层写法：首先明确生存估计的对象、失败事件、删失规则、时间窗和置信区间；其次把全因翻修、排除感染后的柄生存、无菌松动、PROM 和满意度分开。500 例中只有 6 次翻修，五年生存率很高，但没有同期对照；两年 PROM 仅 233 人应答、满意度仅 210 人应答。因而它支持该柄在特定人群中的五年描述性监测，却不直接证明近端负荷、骨量保存、涂层骨长入、骨整合或十年安全性。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference packet section.
Automated case-report, finite-element, and animal cues are false; this is a prospective clinical cohort.
The title says case series, while the methods more precisely support prospective multicenter single-arm cohort.
